name: json
algorithm: Parse a 50 MB JSON document into the std's tree, serialise the tree to compact JSON, parse that text again and walk the second tree; rounds times (README.md).

skip.rust: no std JSON in Rust (serde_json is a crate; no crate stands in)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; parsing has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the checksum is taken over the reparsed values (B18), not the serialised bytes, which differ by library (key order, escapes, number spelling)
notes: B18: the serialised text differs by library (Go sorts map keys and escapes <, > and &; Zig writes its f64 numbers in its own spelling; Mk keeps member order and number text), so the checksum walks the reparsed tree: per value 1 plus the integer part of a number, the decoded length of a string, 3 for true, 5 for false, 7 for null, and per object member 1 plus the key's length.
